title: Seal a runnable verification recipe server-side: give `test` a durable executable body with server-derived argv
description:
PREREQUISITE filed by architect-474a0c03 2026-08-23 at committed HEAD 3537be6, discharging a filing obligation that was ROUTED BUT NEVER EXECUTED. governor-7211ec87's 2026-08-22 handoff on task-d8bb8a985ece4cff953927bbc9c50116 recorded: "durable recipe/brief writer with an explicit executable-command representation -> PREREQUISITE ROW STILL TO BE FILED by architect-a69eb088 with the symbols in comment-bf4da253 (bar 1: this row cannot land without it)". That architect handed off later the same day and the row was never filed. Verified absent before filing: a title scan over every .moe/tasks/*.json for /recipe|mission brief|executable command|argv/ returns exactly ONE row — d8bb8a98 itself. This is not a duplicate.

WHY IT IS NEEDED. task-d8bb8a98 must answer the launch-template producer's exact 4-key mission brief {instructions, test, title, workspace} from committed durable state. Three of the four have at least a candidate durable source. `test` has NONE, and d8bb8a98's own rails forbid every workaround: rail 0 makes launch-template-producer.ts off-limits so the 4-key demand cannot be narrowed, and rail 1 disqualifies spec files, nodeSpecsDir and NodeMission as shared-tree-writable. Its DoD-1 further requires the produced brief be admitted by the REAL produceLaunchTemplateFields on the first try, so a refusal-only producer cannot satisfy it — there must exist at least one world where a genuine `test` value is produced.

MEASURED, SYMBOL BY SYMBOL, AT HEAD 3537be6:

1. RECIPES ARE REFS, NOT BODIES. `NodeDefinition.verificationRecipeRevisions` is `readonly string[]` (packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-authority-contract.ts:154, listed in the key roster at :68), and `AcceptanceContract.obligations[].verificationRecipeRefs` is likewise refs (packages/core/src/planning/acceptance-contract.ts:43,66). `node-authority-compose.ts:106` only checks that every ref is a member of `planning.recipeRefs` — membership, never a body. The only non-test VALUES anywhere are the literal `["recipe-a"]` at apps/daemon/src/planning/journey-authority-bodies.ts:144 and packages/scheduler/src/scheduler-entrypoint-smoke-worker.mjs:157.

2. THE ONLY EXECUTABLE BODY IS UNREACHABLE FROM PRODUCTION. `VerificationRecipe` (packages/runner/src/evidence/verification-recipe.ts:206-236) is the one shape carrying an `argv`. It is sealed by `sealRecipe` (apps/daemon/src/evidence/foundation-verification-service.ts:99-118) from `input.argv` — CALLER-SUPPLIED. `git grep -n sealRecipe -- apps packages` excluding tests returns exactly THREE lines, ALL inside foundation-verification-service.ts itself: :74 the interface member, :99 the definition, :254 its own export in the returned object. There is NO external production call site. So no recipe body exists at dispatch time, and if one did its argv would not be server-derived.

3. THE GAP IS INDEPENDENT OF THE ACTIVE-GRAPH GAP, and must not be folded into it. The active-graph writer gap (all six GRAPH_REVISION_EVENT_KINDS — GraphRevisionActivated/Approved/Created/Rejected/Submitted/Superseded — have ZERO production emitters; the sole non-test hit repo-wide is a COMMENT at apps/daemon/src/planning/active-graph-projection.ts:119) is owned by task-eacea969, currently PLANNING. Landing that writer would give `title` and `instructions` a durable source and would still leave `test` with none, because a graph revision carries recipe REFS. Confirmed with a positive control: the same grep shape finds GoalExecutionEnabled fine (3 hits in admission-gate-resolver.ts), so the empty GraphRevision* result is a real absence rather than a broken grep.

DELIVERABLE. A daemon-side authority that seals a verification recipe whose `argv` is SERVER-DERIVED from committed durable state, and a strict reader that answers the current sealed recipe for a given recipe ref. The seal must have a production call site — an unwired writer passes a symbol grep identically to a wired one and would leave this gap exactly where it is. The representation question the prior audit flagged as unapproved must be DECIDED and STATED in the module: whether the durable body is an argv vector or a shell string, and how it maps to the mission brief's single `test` string. A recipe the authority cannot honestly seal must refuse with a stable code and layer, never default to an empty or placeholder argv.

EXPLICITLY NOT IN SCOPE: producing the mission brief (task-d8bb8a98), retiring the caller-carried launchTemplate (task-fc9660b0), the active-graph transition service (task-eacea969), and editing launch-template-producer.ts or foundation-attempt-* (off-limits under d8bb8a98 rail 0).

implementationPlan.description:
Mutation drills. A green suite is blind to a detached assertion, so each mutant must be SEEN RED before restore.
BEFORE DRILLING: `git status --porcelain` every path you will mutate. All three production modules are NEW and therefore untracked (`??`), and `git diff` is BLIND to untracked paths — an empty diff on a new file certifies nothing, because it is empty before, during and after. For each untracked path take a SHA256 backup outside the tree (under %TEMP%, suffixed by your worker id) and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore; a PowerShell copy can silently no-op and "the command returned" is not evidence the bytes moved.
Run each drill alone — a first red masks a second:
  (a) DELETE THE PRODUCTION CALL SITE (make step 4's module stop calling `sealRecipe`). Step 5 Arm A must go RED. If it stays green the arm is checking export-existence rather than wiring — the precise defect this row was filed to close, and a finding to report rather than a pass.

  (c) CALLER-SUPPLIED ARGV: accept an argv parameter from the caller instead of the reader. The server-derived assertion must red.
  (d) SIZE-AFTER-READ: move the `statSync` ceiling check to after `readFileSync`. The too-large arm must red — proving the ceiling is enforced before the read, not after.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
READ comment-80620701d58846e9a6aa2217f9e85069 FIRST. It carries the argv-source ruling AND AMENDS DoD ITEM 1. As filed, item 1 says the argv must come from "COMMITTED durable state"; the ruled source is host-scoped daemon PROCESS CONFIG, which is not that. A grader reading the field alone will mis-grade this row. The amended requirement: argv derived from SERVER-SIDE AUTHORITY (committed durable state OR host-scoped process config), never a caller payload, spec file or nodeSpecsDir.

WHY THERE IS A RULING AT ALL. This row's rail 4 says to block rather than invent a convention if the argv representation cannot be decided from durable state. I measured that condition and it FIRED: `git grep -nE "\bargv\b" -- packages/core/src packages/scheduler/src apps/daemon/src/planning` excluding tests returns ZERO lines, with a POSITIVE CONTROL against packages/runner/src returning real hits (evidence-contract.ts:194/:204/:222) proving the grep works. `NodeDefinition` (node-authority-contract.ts:140-166) carries objective/capability/constraints/scopes/repositoryBaseTree and `verificationRecipeRevisions` — all REFS, nothing executable. So rather than invent, the question went to the human operator with four measured options; the human chose the host-scoped catalog.

THE PRECEDENT TO MIRROR, LINE BY LINE. The Foundation workspace catalog is the exact shape to copy:
- `FOUNDATION_WORKSPACE_CATALOG_ENV_KEY = "MOE_FOUNDATION_WORKSPACE_CATALOG"` at foundation-capture-lifecycle.ts:132.
- `readFoundationCatalogConfig(env)` at :147-161 returns a LAZY THUNK `() => unknown`. An absent or empty env value returns a thunk yielding `undefined` rather than throwing, so a missing catalog refuses the OPERATION at use time instead of failing daemon boot — daemon-store-dependencies.ts:137-139 states that intent explicitly.
- SIZE IS CHECKED BEFORE THE READ (`statSync(configured).size > MAX_CATALOG_BYTES` at :156), and the comment explains why: reading first and measuring second would pull an operator-sized file into memory to decide it was too large, so the ceiling would exist and protect nothing. Copy this ordering exactly.
- Threading: daemon-store-dependencies.ts:135-137 builds ONE source, read lazily, shared by every consumer "so both resolve the same repository scope authority".
- DECODE AND VALIDATE LIVE IN A SEPARATE MODULE from the reader: foundation-repository-scope-authority.ts (203 lines) holds `refuseCatalog(...)` with codes like FOUNDATION_REPOSITORY_SCOPE_HOST_ROOT_INVALID and FOUNDATION_REPOSITORY_SCOPE_PATH_CASE_COLLISION, validating with `isHostRoot` at :55-58. That split is what keeps both files under the per-file cap.

THE SEAL'S FULL INPUT, and why it is all available pre-dispatch. `FoundationRecipeRegistration` (foundation-verification-contracts.ts:211-218) is {argv, declaredInputs, declaredOutputPaths, recipeAggregateId, runtimeObservation, verifierIdentity}. `runtimeObservation` must be a PROVEN one, which could have been a second causal inversion. It is not:
- `provider.probe` is a SERVED bootstrap command (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:48, CAPABILITIES.ADMIN), handled by `recordProbe` (bootstrap-services.ts:185), admitting a ProviderRuntimeObservation at :154-156 and persisting it at :169 via `providerProbePayload`.
- bootstrap-sequence.ts:34 makes it depend on `project.register`, so it runs at BOOTSTRAP, well before dispatch.
- `provider-runtime-observation-reader.ts` is its durable reader.
So every seal input exists server-side before this row needs it.

sealRecipe ITSELF NEEDS NO CHANGE and must not be edited. foundation-verification-service.ts:99-121 already: builds via `buildVerificationRecipe`, forwards its refusal with `carryEvidenceRefusal(built.code, built.layer)`, answers a re-seal from the DURABLE seal (same sha256 replays, different sha256 refuses FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_RECIPE_CONFLICT under DAEMON_VERIFICATION_IDENTITY), and pins the commit at RECIPE_EXPECTED_VERSION so a race is decided by the store. This row supplies its CALLER, not its behaviour.

ARGV IS A VECTOR, NEVER A SHELL STRING. `buildVerificationRecipe` canonicalises `argv` through `canonicalArgv` (verification-recipe.ts:206-212). A shell string would have to be split by a convention nobody ratified — reintroducing exactly the problem this ruling closes.

RAIL 2 IS NOT WEAKENED. The disqualification of spec files / nodeSpecsDir / NodeMission targets SHARED-TREE-WRITABLE sources: an agent holding the worktree can rewrite them, so they cannot be authority over that agent's own verification. Host process config is outside the worktree and configured by whoever runs the daemon. Same distinction I ruled for `workspace` in comment-9fa4d1ae on task-d8bb8a98.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE WIRED-WRITER TRAP, which is the whole reason this row exists. `sealRecipe` has been present and exported since it was written and has NEVER had a production caller — an unwired writer passes a symbol grep identically to a wired one. DoD item 3 demands a test that asserts the CALL SITE exists, not merely that the symbol is exported. If this row lands a catalog reader and no reachable call site, it has reproduced the exact defect it was filed to close.

2. AN ABSENT CATALOG MUST REFUSE, NEVER DEFAULT. The precedent thunk returns `undefined` when the env key is absent or empty (foundation-capture-lifecycle.ts:151). Downstream that must become a stable refusal code and layer, never an empty argv, never a placeholder, never a caller value. Drill (b) exists to catch a default sneaking in.

3. SIZE BEFORE READ. Copy foundation-capture-lifecycle.ts:153-158's ordering exactly. Reading first and measuring second makes the ceiling decorative.

4. RAIL 2 SOURCE-GREP. DoD item 1's arm greps the module for /node:fs|readFile/ and /nodeSpecsDir|NodeMission/. Same recipeAggregateId + same sha256 = replay answered from the DURABLE seal; same id + different sha256 = FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_RECIPE_CONFLICT under DAEMON_VERIFICATION_IDENTITY. A caller that pre-checks and skips the seal, or that derives a fresh aggregate id per call, silently destroys both properties. Call it and let it answer.

7. PER-FILE CAP. Mirror the precedent's split — contracts/codes in one module, the fs-touching reader in another, the composition in a third. The repository-scope precedent is 203 + 224 lines across two files for the same shape.

8. GATE EXECUTION EVIDENCE. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` exits 0 on zero tests AND on an unresolved package. `@moe/daemon` resolves to apps/daemon. Read the `Test Files N passed` / `Tests N passed` count lines from OUTPUT. Run typecheck and test as SEPARATE legs — never `;`-chained, never piped.

9. DURABLE EVIDENCE SURFACE. `moe.complete_task`'s summary is write-only and persists nowhere. Put the DoD-0 measurement, drill outcomes and gate count lines in a `moe.add_comment`; the summary may only point at it.

10. THE DoD FIELD IS STALE BY DESIGN. Item 1 is amended by comment-80620701d58846e9a6aa2217f9e85069. Cite that comment in the completion record so a strict grader does not reject correct work for not using "committed durable state".
